us-20261017-news-2.title: 中期选举投票率之谜：当白宫不在选票上时，究竟是谁在投票

segments.src: Every four years, American politics seems to take over everything.
segments.tr: 每隔四年，美国政治似乎就会接管一切。

segments.src: Campaign ads, debates, and dinner-table arguments all revolve around one race.
segments.tr: 竞选广告、辩论和餐桌上的争论都围绕着一场竞选展开。

segments.src: Two years later, the energy fades.
segments.tr: 两年后，这股热情便消退了。

segments.src: The offices at stake are still important: all 435 House seats, about a third of the Senate, dozens of governorships, and thousands of state legislative seats.
segments.tr: 处于危险中的职位依然重要：全部 435 个众议院席位、大约三分之一的参议院席位、几十个州长职位以及数千个州议会席位。

segments.src: Yet far fewer people turn out to choose them.
segments.tr: 然而，投票选择这些职位的人却要少得多。

segments.src: This gap between presidential and midterm participation is one of the most reliable patterns in U.S.
segments.tr: 总统大选与中期选举参与度之间的这种差距是美国选举中最可靠的规律之一。

segments.src: elections.
segments.tr: elections.

segments.src: It also shapes which candidates win, which issues get attention, and how each party plans its campaigns.
segments.tr: 它还决定了哪些候选人获胜、哪些议题受到关注，以及各政党如何规划其竞选活动。

segments.src: ## How Big Is the Gap?
segments.tr: ## 差距有多大？

segments.src: In recent decades, turnout in midterm elections has usually run well below turnout in presidential years.
segments.tr: 近几十年来，中期选举的投票率通常远低于总统大选年。

segments.src: Typically, somewhere around 40 to 50 percent of eligible voters cast ballots in a midterm, compared with roughly 55 to 66 percent in a presidential election.
segments.tr: 通常情况下，中期选举中大约有 40% 到 50% 的合格选民投票，而总统大选中这一比例约为 55% 到 66%。

segments.src: The 2018 and 2022 midterms were notable exceptions to the long-running trend of low participation.
segments.tr: 2018 年和 2022 年的中期选举打破了长期低参与度的趋势，成为了显著的例外。

segments.src: Both drew historically high turnout for a midterm, with 2018 reaching about 50 percent of eligible voters, the highest rate in roughly a century.
segments.tr: 这两次选举都吸引了中期选举历史上极高的投票率，其中 2018 年达到了约 50% 的合格选民投票率，创下了一个世纪以来的最高纪录。

segments.src: Even so, those elections still fell short of the presidential contests that bracketed them.
segments.tr: 即便如此，这些选举仍未达到将其夹在中间的总统大选的水平。

segments.src: The "drop-off" between presidential and midterm years has narrowed in some cases, but it has not disappeared.
segments.tr: 总统大选年与中期选举年之间的“投票率下降”现象在某些情况下有所缩小，但并未消失。

segments.src: ## Who Shows Up
segments.tr: ## 谁会出来投票

segments.src: Midterm electorates are not just smaller versions of presidential electorates.
segments.tr: 中期选举的选民群体并非总统大选选民群体的简单缩小版。

segments.src: They differ in composition.
segments.tr: 它们的构成有所不同。

segments.src: **Older voters are overrepresented.** Voting rates rise steadily with age.
segments.tr: **老年选民的代表性过高。** 投票率随年龄增长而稳步上升。

segments.src: Adults over 65 vote at much higher rates than adults under 30 in every election, but the difference widens in midterm years.
segments.tr: 在每次选举中，65 岁以上成人的投票率都远高于 30 岁以下的成人，但在中期选举年，这种差距会进一步扩大。

segments.src: In a presidential year, a surge of younger and first-time voters partly offsets this imbalance.
segments.tr: 在总统大选年，年轻选民和首次投票选民的涌入在一定程度上抵消了这种不平衡。

segments.src: In a midterm, that surge is smaller.
segments.tr: 但在中期选举中，这种涌入较小。

segments.src: **Habitual and partisan voters dominate.** People who vote in every election, including low-profile ones, tend to be more politically engaged and more strongly attached to a party.
segments.tr: **习惯性选民和党派选民占主导地位。** 每次选举（包括低关注度的选举）都投票的人，通常政治参与度更高，对政党的黏性也更强。

segments.src: Occasional voters, who often decide to participate only when a presidential race raises the stakes, are more likely to sit out.
segments.tr: 而偶尔投票的选民往往只在总统竞选提高赌注时才决定参与，他们更有可能选择作壁上观。

segments.src: **Education and income matter.** Voters with college degrees and higher household incomes participate at higher rates than others, and these differences also grow in midterm years.
segments.tr: **教育程度和收入至关重要。** 拥有大学学位和较高家庭收入的选民参与率高于其他人，而且这种差距在中期选举年也会扩大。

segments.src: Homeowners and people who have lived in the same community for a long time are likewise more likely to vote than renters and recent movers.
segments.tr: 房主和在同一社区居住较长时间的人也比租房者和最近搬家的人更有可能投票。

segments.src: ## Who Stays Home
segments.tr: ## 谁选择留在家中

segments.src: The people most likely to skip a midterm include younger adults, newly registered voters, those with lower incomes, and those with less connection to local community institutions.
segments.tr: 最有可能跳过中期选举的人包括年轻人、新注册选民、低收入群体以及与当地社区机构联系较少的人。

segments.src: Surveys regularly find several reasons:
segments.tr: 调查经常发现以下几个原因：

segments.src: - **Low awareness.** Many people simply don't know a midterm is happening, or know little about the candidates on the ballot.
segments.tr: - **低意识。** 许多人根本不知道中期选举正在发生，或者对选票上的候选人知之甚少。

segments.src: - **Practical barriers.** Work schedules, caregiving duties, transportation, and registration deadlines can all make voting harder, especially when it feels less urgent.
segments.tr: - **现实障碍。** 工作时间表、照顾他人的责任、交通和注册截止日期都会使投票变得更加困难，尤其是当投票感觉没有那么紧迫时。

segments.src: - **Lower perceived stakes.** Without a presidential contest, some people feel their vote matters less, even though many of the decisions that most directly affect daily life are made by state and local officials.
segments.tr: - **感知的 stakes 较低。** 没有了总统竞选，有些人会觉得他们的投票不那么重要，尽管许多直接影响日常生活的大部分决策都是由州和地方官员做出的。

segments.src: - **Disillusionment.** Some non-voters say they feel neither party speaks to them.
segments.tr: - **幻灭感。** 一些不投票的人表示，他们觉得没有哪个政党能代表他们的心声。

segments.src: ## Why the Gap Matters Politically
segments.tr: ## 为什么这个差距在政治上很重要

segments.src: Because the midterm electorate is older, more engaged, and more partisan, campaign strategy changes.
segments.tr: 由于中期选举的选民年龄更大、参与度更高、党派色彩更浓，竞选策略也随之发生了变化。

segments.src: Candidates and party organizations focus less on persuading undecided voters and more on motivating their committed supporters to show up.
segments.tr: 候选人和政党组织减少了对说服未决选民的关注，转而更多地激发他们坚定的支持者出来投票。

segments.src: A party whose supporters are enthusiastic can benefit from a strong turnout of its base even if its overall support is no larger than the other side's.
segments.tr: 如果一个政党的支持者热情高涨，即使其实际总体支持率并不比对方大，也能从其基石选民的高投票率中获益。

segments.src: The president's party also has a well-documented disadvantage.
segments.tr: 总统所在的政党也存在一个有据可查的劣势。

segments.src: In most midterm elections since the end of World War II, the party holding the White House has lost seats in the House of Representatives.
segments.tr: 自二战结束以来的大多数中期选举中，掌控白宫的政党都在众议院失去了席位。

segments.src: Political scientists offer several explanations: voters who are dissatisfied with the current administration may be more motivated to vote than those who are content, and the presidential "coattails" that help candidates in a presidential year are absent.
segments.tr: 政治学家给出了几种解释：对现任政府不满的选民可能比感到满意的选民更有投票动力，并且总统在总统大选中帮助候选人的“光环效应”此时并不存在。

segments.src: Turnout is not the only factor.
segments.tr: 投票率并不是唯一的因素。

segments.src: Economic conditions, the president's approval rating, redistricting, candidate quality, and the national mood all play major roles.
segments.tr: 经济状况、总统的支持率、选区划分、候选人质量以及国家情绪都发挥着重要作用。

segments.src: Studies have also found that high turnout does not always favor one party.
segments.tr: 研究还发现，高投票率并不总是对某一个政党有利。

segments.src: The effect depends on which groups are mobilized in a given year and place.
segments.tr: 这种效果取决于在特定年份和特定地点动员了哪些群体。

segments.src: ## Closing the Gap
segments.tr: ## 缩小差距

segments.src: Election administrators, civic groups, and campaigns have tried many approaches to boost participation in off-year elections:
segments.tr: 选举管理人员、公民团体和竞选活动尝试了许多方法来提高非大选年的参与度：

segments.src: - Early voting, mail voting, and extended hours to give voters more flexibility
segments.tr: - 提前投票、邮寄投票和延长投票时间，为选民提供更多灵活性

segments.src: - Automatic or same-day voter registration in some states
segments.tr: - 在一些州实行自动或当日选民登记

segments.src: - Nonpartisan outreach that explains what offices are on the ballot and what they do
segments.tr: - 无党派的外展活动，解释选票上有哪些职位以及它们的职责是什么

segments.src: - Reminders and community-based efforts to reach first-time and infrequent voters
segments.tr: - 通过提醒和社区化的努力来接触首次投票和不常投票的选民

segments.src: Research suggests that simple, personal contact, such as a neighbor or volunteer encouraging someone to vote, can make a measurable difference.
segments.tr: 研究表明，简单、个人的接触，例如邻居或志愿者鼓励某人投票，可以产生可衡量的影响。

segments.src: The effects are modest per person, but they add up in close races.
segments.tr: 这种影响对个人而言虽然不大，但在势均力敌的竞选中却能积少成多。

segments.src: ## The Takeaway
segments.tr: ## 核心要点

segments.src: The midterm turnout puzzle comes down to a basic fact: the people who decide midterm elections are not a perfect mirror of the country.
segments.tr: 中期选举投票率之谜归结为一个基本事实：决定中期选举结果的人并非这个国家的完美缩影。

segments.src: Those who vote are older, more partisan, and more consistently engaged than those who don't.
segments.tr: 投票的人比不投票的人年龄更大、党派色彩更浓且参与度更持续。

segments.src: That reality affects campaign messaging, party fortunes, and ultimately the policies that follow.
segments.tr: 这种现实影响着竞选信息传递、政党命运以及最终随之而来的政策。

segments.src: For voters, the lesson is simple.
segments.tr: 对于选民来说，这个教训很简单。

segments.src: Elections with lower turnout give each individual ballot more weight.
segments.tr: 投票率较低的选举让每张选票都拥有更大的分量。

segments.src: For anyone curious about how their community is represented, checking registration status, learning what's on the ballot, and making a plan to vote are practical first steps.
segments.tr: 对于任何对自己的社区如何被代表感到好奇的人来说，检查注册状态、了解选票内容并制定投票计划是切实可行的第一步。

segments.src: Election dates, polling places, and deadlines can be confirmed through your state or local election office.
segments.tr: 选举日期、投票地点和截止日期可以通过您所在的州或地方选举办公室进行确认。

segments.src: *This article is for general informational purposes and does not endorse any candidate or party.
segments.tr: *本文仅供一般参考之用，不背书任何候选人或政党。

segments.src: Turnout figures are approximate and vary by source and year.*
segments.tr: 投票率数据为近似值，会因来源和年份而异。*

us-20261017-news-1.title: 11月1日时钟拨回一小时：为什么美国依然无法就停止调时达成一致

segments.src: In the early hours of **Sunday, November 1**, most of the United States will turn its clocks back one hour and return to standard time.
segments.tr: 在**11月1日，星期日**的清晨，美国大部分地区将把时钟拨慢一小时，恢复标准时间。

segments.src: Many people will enjoy an extra hour of sleep.
segments.tr: 许多人将享受额外一小时的睡眠。

segments.src: Many will also be asking a familiar question: why are we still doing this?
segments.tr: 许多人也会提出一个熟悉的问题：为什么我们仍在这样做？

segments.src: Efforts to end the twice-a-year clock change have drawn support from both parties, from the White House and from large parts of the public.
segments.tr: 终止每年两次调时工作的努力得到了两党、白宫以及大部分公众的支持。

segments.src: Legislation to make daylight saving time permanent has stalled in Congress again.
segments.tr: 使夏令时永久化的法案再次在国会搁浅。

segments.src: Here is where the debate stands, what research says, and why states can't simply settle the matter themselves.
segments.tr: 以下是辩论现状、研究结论，以及为什么各州无法自行解决这一问题。

segments.src: ## How the current system works
segments.tr: ## 当前系统如何运作

segments.src: The Uniform Time Act of 1966 created a national framework for daylight saving time (DST).
segments.tr: 1966 年的《统一时间法案》为夏令时（DST）建立了全国性框架。

segments.src: Under today's rules, DST runs from the second Sunday in March to the first Sunday in November.
segments.tr: 根据现行规则，夏令时从 3 月的第二个星期日持续到 11 月的第一个星期日。

segments.src: States have limited choices under that law:
segments.tr: 在该法律下，各州的选择有限：

segments.src: - **They can stay on standard time all year.** Hawaii and most of Arizona do this, along with several U.S. territories.
segments.tr: - **他们可以全年实行标准时间。** 夏威夷州和亚利桑那州的大部分地区，以及若干美国领地都是如此。

segments.src: - **They cannot adopt permanent daylight saving time on their own.** That change requires an act of Congress.
segments.tr: - **他们不能自行采用永久夏令时。** 这一变更需要国会通过法案。

segments.src: Roughly twenty states have passed laws or resolutions that would adopt year-round daylight saving time if Congress permits it.
segments.tr: 大约有 20 个州已经通过了法律或决议，如果国会允许，他们将采用全年夏令时。

segments.src: Those measures sit idle until federal law changes.
segments.tr: 在联邦法律修改之前，这些措施一直处于闲置状态。

segments.src: ## Why the push has stalled
segments.tr: ## 为什么推动陷入停滞

segments.src: The best-known proposal is the Sunshine Protection Act, which would lock in daylight time year-round.
segments.tr: 最著名的提议是《阳光保护法案》，该法案将全年锁定夏令时。

segments.src: The Senate passed a version by unanimous consent in 2022, but it never received a vote in the House.
segments.tr: 参议院于 2022 年通过一致同意方式通过了一个版本，但该版本从未在众议院接受表决。

segments.src: Versions have been reintroduced in later sessions, and public statements of support from political leaders have followed.
segments.tr: 后续会期中重新引入了相关版本，政治领导人也发表了公开支持声明。

segments.src: Still, no bill has reached the president's desk.
segments.tr: 尽管如此，仍未有任何法案送交总统签署。

segments.src: Several things keep the issue stuck:
segments.tr: 有几点原因导致该议题卡住：

segments.src: 1. **Disagreement over which time to make permanent.** Supporters of permanent daylight time want long summer-style evenings all year. Many sleep scientists argue permanent *standard* time is the better choice. Those two camps split the reform coalition.
segments.tr: 1. **关于将哪种时间永久化的分歧。** 永久夏令时的支持者希望全年拥有漫长的夏季风格傍晚。许多睡眠科学家主张永久*标准*时间是更好的选择。这两个阵营分化了改革联盟。

segments.src: 2. **Regional differences.** Sunrise and sunset times vary widely across the country. Permanent daylight time would mean very late winter sunrises in some northern and western areas of a time zone.
segments.tr: 2. **区域差异。** 全国各地的日出和日落时间差异很大。永久夏令时意味着时区内一些北部和西部地区的冬日日出会非常晚。

segments.src: 3. **Limited floor time.** Congress has many competing priorities, and a change that touches every clock in the country is easy to postpone.
segments.tr: 3. **有限的议场审议时间。** 国会面临许多相互竞争的优先事项，而一项涉及全国每一个时钟的变更很容易被推迟。

segments.src: ## What the sleep evidence says
segments.tr: ## 睡眠研究证据说了什么

segments.src: Major sleep medicine organizations, including the American Academy of Sleep Medicine, have called for eliminating seasonal clock changes.
segments.tr: 包括美国睡眠医学会在内的主要睡眠医学机构呼吁取消季节性调时。

segments.src: Their preferred option is permanent standard time, because it more closely matches the body's natural light-dark cycle.
segments.tr: 他们首选的方案是永久标准时间，因为它更符合人体自然的昼夜光照节律。

segments.src: Researchers have linked the spring shift, when we lose an hour, to short-term disruptions such as less sleep and more daytime drowsiness.
segments.tr: 研究人员将春季切换（丢失一小时）与短期干扰联系起来，例如睡眠减少和白天昏昏欲睡增加。

segments.src: Some studies have also found small, temporary increases in heart attack and stroke risk in the days after the spring change.
segments.tr: 一些研究还发现，在春季调时后的几天里，心肌梗死和中风风险有轻微的短暂增加。

segments.src: These findings describe averages across large populations, not a risk that every individual will experience, but they are a main reason health groups favor ending the switch.
segments.tr: 这些发现描述的是庞人群的平均状况，并非每个人都会经历的风险，但它们是健康团体主张停止调时的主要原因。

segments.src: ## Safety and energy
segments.tr: ## 安全与能源

segments.src: The safety picture is mixed.
segments.tr: 安全方面的状况喜忧参半。

segments.src: Evening daylight can reduce some crimes and traffic collisions involving pedestrians at dusk.
segments.tr: 傍晚的日光可以减少黄昏时分涉及行人的某些犯罪和交通碰撞。

segments.src: Darker winter mornings under permanent daylight time could raise risks for children walking to school and for early commuters.
segments.tr: 在永久夏令时下，更黑暗的冬季早晨可能会增加步行上学的儿童和早期通勤者的风险。

segments.src: Research on crash rates after clock changes has also found short-lived spikes, especially after the spring change.
segments.tr: 对调时后事故率的研究也发现存在短暂的峰值，尤其是在春季调时之后。

segments.src: The original energy-saving argument is weaker than many assume.
segments.tr: 最初的节约能源论点比许多人假设的要弱。

segments.src: Modern studies generally find the effect on electricity use is small, and in some regions it is close to zero, because heating, cooling and electronics use have changed since the policy began.
segments.tr: 现代研究普遍发现，对用电量的影响微乎其微，在某些地区几乎为零，因为自该政策实施以来，供暖、冷却和电子设备的使用已发生改变。

segments.src: ## The economic argument
segments.tr: ## 经济论点

segments.src: Business groups, retailers and the recreation and tourism sectors have often backed more evening daylight, arguing that people shop and spend more when it is light after work.
segments.tr: 商业团体、零售商以及娱乐和旅游部门通常支持增加傍晚日光，认为人们在下班后天亮时会进行更多购物和消费。

segments.src: Others point to costs from lost productivity after the spring change and from the confusion of coordinating schedules across time zones, especially in transportation, broadcasting and finance.
segments.tr: 其他人则指出春季切换后生产力下降带来的成本，以及跨时区协调日程安排（特别是在运输、广播和金融领域）所引发的混乱成本。

segments.src: Estimates of the economic effect vary a great deal depending on the method used, so they should be treated with caution.
segments.tr: 对经济影响的评估因所用方法的不同而差异很大，因此应谨慎对待。

segments.src: ## The lesson of the 1970s
segments.tr: ## 1970年代的教训

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 美国

segments.src: has tried this before.
segments.tr: 以前尝试过这种做法。

segments.src: In 1974, Congress approved year-round daylight time as an energy-saving experiment.
segments.tr: 1974 年，国会批准了全年夏令时作为一项节能实验。

segments.src: Public support dropped during the first dark winter mornings, and Congress repealed the measure the next year.
segments.tr: 在最初几个黑暗的冬季早晨，公众支持率下降，国会在次年废除了该措施。

segments.src: That history is a major reason lawmakers and scientists urge care about which permanent time to choose.
segments.tr: 这段历史是立法者和科学家呼吁对选择哪种永久时间保持谨慎的主要原因。

segments.src: ## What to expect this November
segments.tr: ## 今年 11 月可以期待什么

segments.src: For now, nothing changes in law.
segments.tr: 目前，法律没有任何改变。

segments.src: Sunrise and sunset will shift an hour earlier on November 1, and evenings will get dark sooner.
segments.tr: 11 月 1 日的日出和日落将提前一小时，傍晚天黑得更早。

segments.src: Some practical steps can ease the adjustment:
segments.tr: 一些实用步骤可以缓解这种适应过程：

segments.src: - Shift bedtime 15 to 20 minutes earlier for a few nights beforehand.
segments.tr: - 在此之前提前几天将睡觉时间提前 15 到 20 分钟。

segments.src: - Get outdoor light in the morning after the change.
segments.tr: - 在调整后的早晨接受户外光照。

segments.src: - Keep meal and wake-up times steady.
segments.tr: - 保持固定的用餐和起床时间。

segments.src: - Take extra care when driving at dusk, when drivers and pedestrians are adjusting to earlier darkness.
segments.tr: - 在黄昏驾驶时格外小心，此时驾驶员和行人正在适应更早到来的黑夜。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: Americans say in surveys that they want an end to clock changes, but they are less united on which time to keep.
segments.tr: 美国人在调查中表示他们希望停止调时，但对于保留哪种时间意见不太统一。

segments.src: Until Congress picks one, and until states get the option or the mandate to act, the clocks will keep moving twice a year.
segments.tr: 在国会做出选择、且各州获得采取行动的选择权或授权之前，时钟每年仍将移动两次。

segments.src: Meanwhile, the evidence supports one clear conclusion: whichever time is chosen, staying on it all year is likely to be better than switching back and forth.
segments.tr: 同时，证据支持一个明确的结论：无论选择哪种时间，全年保持不变可能都比来回切换更好。

segments.src: *This article is for general information and does not constitute medical advice.
segments.tr: *本文仅供参考，不构成医疗建议。

segments.src: People with sleep or health concerns should speak with a qualified health professional.*
segments.tr: 有睡眠或健康疑虑的人应咨询合格的医疗专业人员。*

us-20261017-news-3.title: 感恩节餐桌账单：今年的火鸡、填料和派可能需要多少钱

segments.src: With Thanksgiving about five weeks away, the cost of the holiday meal is already a popular topic at kitchen tables and in grocery aisles.
segments.tr: 距离感恩节还有大约五周的时间，节日大餐的成本已经成为餐桌旁和超市走廊里热门的讨论话题。

segments.src: Households that host a big dinner often start planning early, and many want to know whether the familiar menu of turkey, stuffing, vegetables and pie will cost more or less than last year.
segments.tr: 举办大型晚宴的家庭通常会尽早开始规划，许多人都想知道，由火鸡、填料、蔬菜和派组成的熟悉菜单，其开销会比去年更高还是更低。

segments.src: This guide explains what tends to drive the price of the main ingredients and how to read the annual dinner-cost surveys without over-interpreting a single headline number.
segments.tr: 本指南解释了通常导致主要食材价格波动的因素，以及如何在不过度解读单一标题数字的情况下看待每年的晚餐成本调查。

segments.src: It does not predict exact prices.
segments.tr: 它并不预测确切的价格。

segments.src: Costs vary by region, store and week.
segments.tr: 成本因地区、商店和周次而异。

segments.src: ## Why Thanksgiving Prices Get So Much Attention
segments.tr: ## 为什么感恩节价格如此受关注

segments.src: Thanksgiving is one of the few meals in the United States built around a nearly standard menu.
segments.tr: 感恩节是美国少数几个围绕近乎标准菜单构建的节日餐食之一。

segments.src: That makes it a convenient yardstick.
segments.tr: 这使其成为一个方便的衡量基准。

segments.src: Because most households buy a similar set of items, changes in the total are easy to compare from one year to the next.
segments.tr: 由于大多数家庭购买的商品组合相似，因此总额的变化很容易在不同年份之间进行比较。

segments.src: The meal also stands in for broader grocery inflation, so a rise or fall in the "dinner bill" often shapes conversations about everyday food costs.
segments.tr: 这顿大餐也代表了更广泛的食品杂货通货膨胀，因此“晚餐账单”的涨跌往往会影响人们对日常食品成本的讨论。

segments.src: ## Turkey: Supply, Disease and Timing
segments.tr: ## 火鸡：供应、疾病与时机

segments.src: The turkey is usually the most expensive single item, and its price depends on several factors:
segments.tr: 火鸡通常是最昂贵的单项商品，其价格取决于几个因素：

segments.src: - **Flock size.** Producers decide months ahead how many birds to raise. Outbreaks of avian influenza can shrink flocks and tighten supply, which has pushed turkey prices up in past years.
segments.tr: - **种群规模。** 生产商提前数月决定养殖多少羽家禽。禽流感的爆发可能会缩减禽群并紧缩供应，这在过去几年曾推高火鸡价格。

segments.src: - **Feed and energy costs.** Grain prices, fuel and processing expenses all feed into the final shelf price.
segments.tr: - **饲料和能源成本。** 粮食价格、燃料和加工费用都会反映在最终的上架价格中。

segments.src: - **Retail strategy.** Many grocery chains treat turkey as a "loss leader." They discount it heavily, sometimes in exchange for a minimum purchase, to bring shoppers into the store.
segments.tr: - **零售策略。** 许多超市连锁店将火鸡视为“引流亏本商品”（loss leader）。他们会大幅打折，有时以最低消费额为条件，以吸引顾客光顾商店。

segments.src: - **Timing.** Frozen turkeys are often cheapest in the weeks right before the holiday, while fresh birds usually cost more per pound.
segments.tr: - **购买时机。** 冻火鸡通常在节日前的几周内最便宜，而新鲜火鸡按磅计算通常更贵。

segments.src: ## Dairy: Butter, Cream and Milk
segments.tr: ## 乳制品：黄油、奶油和牛奶

segments.src: Dairy shows up in mashed potatoes, casseroles, rolls and pie fillings.
segments.tr: 乳制品广泛应用于土豆泥、砂锅菜、小面包和派馅中。

segments.src: Prices follow milk supply, feed costs, seasonal demand and trade conditions.
segments.tr: 价格取决于牛奶供应、饲料成本、季节性需求和贸易状况。

segments.src: Butter and cream tend to be more volatile than milk, and demand rises sharply in the weeks around the holidays.
segments.tr: 黄油和奶油往往比牛奶的价格波动更大，并且需求在节日临近的前后几周内剧增。

segments.src: Store brands are often noticeably cheaper than name brands for the same ingredient.
segments.tr: 对于相同的食材，自有品牌通常明显比知名品牌更便宜。

segments.src: ## Produce: Weather and Transportation
segments.tr: ## 农产品：天气与运输

segments.src: Fresh vegetables, cranberries, sweet potatoes and potatoes are sensitive to weather, harvest conditions and transportation costs.
segments.tr: 新鲜蔬菜、蔓越莓、红薯和土豆对天气、收成状况和运输成本非常敏感。

segments.src: A poor growing season in one region can lift prices nationally, while a strong harvest can keep them steady.
segments.tr: 一个地区的糟糕生长季可能会推高全国范围内的价格，而丰收则能维持价格稳定。

segments.src: Canned and frozen versions of many items are often cheaper and last longer, which makes them a practical option for the side dishes.
segments.tr: 许多商品的罐装和冻干版本通常更便宜且保质期更长，这使其成为配菜的实用选择。

segments.src: ## Stuffing, Rolls and Pie
segments.tr: ## 填料、小面包和派

segments.src: Packaged stuffing mix, bread, flour, sugar and pie crusts depend largely on wheat, sugar and packaging costs.
segments.tr: 包装好的填料混合料、面包、面粉、糖和派皮很大程度上取决于小麦、糖和包装成本。

segments.src: Pumpkin and pecan pie ingredients can swing with crop conditions.
segments.tr: 南瓜派和山核桃派的原料会随着作物状况而波动。

segments.src: Many shoppers save money by baking from scratch, while others find a store-bought pie cheaper once their time and extra ingredients are counted.
segments.tr: 许多顾客通过从头自己烘焙来省钱，而另一些人则发现，如果算上时间和额外食材，购买现成的派反而更便宜。

segments.src: ## How to Read the Annual Dinner-Cost Surveys
segments.tr: ## 如何解读每年的晚餐成本调查

segments.src: Several organizations publish a yearly estimate of the cost of a Thanksgiving dinner.
segments.tr: 一些机构每年都会发布一份感恩节晚餐成本的估算。

segments.src: The best known is the American Farm Bureau Federation's survey, which prices a classic menu for a set number of guests, typically ten, using reports from volunteer shoppers across the country.
segments.tr: 最知名的是美国农场局联合会（American Farm Bureau Federation）的调查，该调查利用来自全国各地志愿者顾客的报告，对设定人数（通常为 10 人）的经典菜单进行定价。

segments.src: Some retailers and consumer groups publish their own versions.
segments.tr: 一些零售商和消费者团体也会发布他们自己的版本。

segments.src: A few points help put these numbers in context:
segments.tr: 以下几点有助于将这些数字置于具体语境中理解：

segments.src: 1. **Check the menu.** Surveys price a specific list of items. If your table has more dishes, different dishes or a larger crowd, your total will differ.
segments.tr: 1. **核对菜单。** 调查是对特定商品清单进行定价。如果你的餐桌上有更多菜肴、不同的菜肴或更多的客人，你的总开销就会有所不同。

segments.src: 2. **Look at the method.** Some surveys use regular shelf prices, while others include promotions. Results can differ by several dollars for that reason alone.
segments.tr: 2. **查看方法。** 一些调查使用常规上架价格，而另一些则包含促销优惠。仅凭这一点，结果就可能相差几美元。

segments.src: 3. **Compare like with like.** A survey from one organization is not directly comparable to a survey from another.
segments.tr: 3. **同类对比。** 来自一个机构的调查与来自另一个机构的调查不可直接进行比较。

segments.src: 4. **Remember it's an average.** Prices in a big city, a rural town and a discount grocer can differ widely.
segments.tr: 4. **记住这是一个平均值。** 大城市、乡村小镇和折扣超市的价格可能会大不相同。

segments.src: 5. **Watch the trend, not the decimal.** A small change from last year may not mean much. A larger shift, and what caused it, is more informative.
segments.tr: 5. **看趋势，而不是小数点。** 与去年相比的小幅变化可能并没有多大意义。更大的转变以及导致转变的原因更有参考价值。

segments.src: 6. **Note the timing.** Prices are collected weeks before the holiday, and store sales may change what you actually pay.
segments.tr: 6. **注意时间点。** 价格数据是在节日到来前数周收集的，而门店促销可能会改变你实际支付的金额。

segments.src: ## Practical Ways to Keep the Bill in Check
segments.tr: ## 控费的实用方法

segments.src: - **Make a menu and a list first.** Planning cuts impulse purchases and food waste.
segments.tr: - **先列菜单和购物清单。** 提前规划可以减少冲动消费和食物浪费。

segments.src: - **Compare unit prices.** The price per pound or per ounce shows the real value better than the sticker price.
segments.tr: - **比较单价。** 每磅或每盎司的价格比标价更能反映真实价值。

segments.src: - **Use store promotions and loyalty programs,** but check whether a turkey deal requires a minimum spend.
segments.tr: - **利用门店促销和会员计划，** 但要核对火鸡优惠是否要求达到最低消费额。

segments.src: - **Consider alternatives.** A smaller bird, a turkey breast or a different main dish can lower costs for a smaller group.
segments.tr: - **考虑替代方案。** 对于人数较少的聚会，更小的火鸡、火鸡胸肉或不同的主菜可以降低成本。

segments.src: - **Buy shelf-stable items early** and watch for sales on baking staples.
segments.tr: - **提早购买耐贮存商品，** 并密切关注烘焙必需品的打折信息。

segments.src: - **Share the load.** Asking guests to bring a side dish or dessert spreads out the expense.
segments.tr: - **分担费用。** 让客人自带一道配菜或甜点可以分散开支。

segments.src: - **Plan for leftovers** so less food goes to waste.
segments.tr: - **计划处理剩菜，** 从而减少食物浪费。

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: Nobody can say exactly what your Thanksgiving table will cost until you are at the checkout.
segments.tr: 在你结账之前，没有人能准确说出你的感恩节餐桌要花多少钱。

segments.src: Still, understanding what moves the price of turkey, dairy and produce, and knowing how the annual surveys are built, can help you separate real trends from headlines.
segments.tr: 尽管如此，了解影响火鸡、乳制品和农产品价格波动的因素，并了解年度调查是如何制作的，有助于你从新闻标题中分辨出真正的趋势。

segments.src: A little planning and some comparison shopping will usually do more for your budget than any national average.
segments.tr: 相比任何全国平均水准，一点点规划和一些比价购物通常能为你的预算带来更多实惠。

segments.src: *This article is for general information only and is not financial advice.
segments.tr: *本文仅供一般信息参考，不构成财务建议。

segments.src: Prices vary by location and retailer.*
segments.tr: 价格因地点和零售商而异。*
